speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) why did Singapore abstain from voting on the International Labour Organization's (ILO)’s Convention on Workplace Violence and Harassment despite its comprehensive coverage; and (b) whether the Government plans to ratify the Convention.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for Manpower regarding Singapore's abstention from the ILO vote on the Violence and Harassment Convention 2019 (a) whether the Government agrees with the general spirit of the Convention; and (b) what are the Government's plans to deal with the issues leading to its decision to abstain from the ILO vote.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Adoption of a Convention by the ILO does not mean that all states will automatically ratify it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Among the Conventions adopted since the year 2000, few have been ratified by more than 25% of the ILO member states.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We have a long-standing policy to only consider adopting or ratifying Conventions which are in Singapore’s interests and with which our laws and policies can fully comply.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the meantime, where we have doubts, we will continue to study the terms of the Convention.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the meantime, we will also make improvements to our policies and measures that are aligned with the spirit of the Convention, if they also meet our objectives.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: A good example is the ILO’s Occupational Safety and Health Convention, or Convention 155, which we ratified recently.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Well before we did, Singapore took steps to strengthen our measures and successfully reduced workplace fatality rates.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For example, it proposes measures, such as including domestic violence in workplace risk assessments.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This would expand workplace safety and health well beyond the workplace remit.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We continue to partner the ILO to promote decent work and have put in place practical measures to eliminate workplace violence and harassment.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Today, employers must already meet the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices, which covers grievance handling.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Among other things, employers are required to respond promptly to affected persons and conduct proper investigations into complaints.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Employers who need help may also approach the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) for help to put in place processes to manage workplace harassment complaints.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In addition, concerned employees may also approach TAFEP for advice and assistance through its hotline, email or writing in.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Where appropriate, TAFEP will refer cases to Government agencies and partners, including the Police and the Courts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Egregious cases, such as the outrage of modesty, are punishable offences under the Penal Code, or can be taken up under the Protection from Harassment Act.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The first is, I understand ILO is made up of different tripartite members, but in terms of the states, there are only six states which have abstained.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: We are one, including countries like Russia, Kyrgyzstan, El Salvador, Malaysia and Paraguay, I think.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: So, pardon me if I got the countries wrong.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: How many of these tripartite partners from Singapore voted for, against or also abstained, along with the Government?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The second question is: I understand there are some concerns with the Convention that we have abstained from ratifying.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: What are we doing in the meantime to get us to be more comfortable with those terms and guidelines that we are not yet comfortable for full ratification?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The third question is whether the Ministry has any plans to look at companies or employers being liable to create a workplace harassment-free environment.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: If companies and organisations are already liable for solvency, they are also entitled to protection against harassment in our recent Protection from Harassment Act, then I find it really difficult to see that they cannot be liable for making sure that the workplace is free from harassment and violence.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As I had outlined, we take practical measures.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As I had mentioned in my earlier reply, the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices does impose certain requirements on the employers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If they do not know how to implement these obligations, we make ourselves available to help them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If their employees find that these measures that are in place are not sufficient, we are also quite happy to step in.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And if there are specific instances where the employees feel that their employers did not help to resolve harassment or even violence 	at the workplace, we certainly will take a very serious view into rectifying this.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is not to trivialise the concerns of those who did file the complaints.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But in general, we do not have a pervasive issue.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is quite specific to certain employers, certain types of work arrangements.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I think that also addresses the third question: what are employers liable for?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Coming back to the Member's first question, which are the parties that abstained or how did we vote, amongst the Singapore delegation.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Singapore delegation comprises the Government, as well as our employers' representatives and, of course, our Labour Movement.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Because this Convention has been in negotiation for about two years, the positions of each of our tripartite partners in Singapore are well known to one another.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I just want to ask, moving forward, whether the Ministry of Manpower will consider including in the tripartite standard some guidelines on how employers can help employees who are facing domestic violence.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I am not so sure that the answer is so clear for everyone.
